newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge criticizes Peruvian's immigration case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge criticizes Peruvian's immigration case.

text.p: By Gail Appleson, U.S. Law Correspondent
A federal judge lambasted U.S. immigration officials and prosecutors on Tuesday for keeping a Peruvian national in prison for six months after an immigration judge ruled he could be released.

U.S. District Judge Lewis Kaplan made his comments during a hearing at which a lawyer for Julian Calero Salazar sought the Peruvian's release pending a decision by immigration officials on his client's request for political asylum.

Peru had sought Calero Salazar's extradition, alleging he was a member of the leftist guerrilla group Shining Path. However, Calero Salazar's lawyer Michael Deutsch has argued that the charge was contrived and his client fled Peru because of political persecution and fear of the military police.
Deutsch, legal director for the Centre of Constitutional Rights, said Calero Salazar's wife and father-in-law have been jailed and tortured and his brother-in-law killed.
Kaplan reserved decision but harshly criticised U.S. officials for delaying the case for many months.

He told federal prosecutors that since his three years on the bench, he had seen the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service act in a "disasterous fashion" on more than one occasion, "But this one takes the cake and I'm not going to stand for it much longer."
"It's outrageous what's taken place," he said.
The judge said that the government claimed the case was being handled on an expedited basis. "This is about as expedited as a glacier going uphill," the judge said.

Federal prosecutors ended extraditon proceeding in August when Peru failed to supply sufficient evidence against Calero Salazar. An immigration judge granted bail on Sept. 6 after finding that Calero Salazar posed no risk of flight or danger to the community.

But the INS won a temporary stay of the ruling from the Board of Immigration Appeals while it determined if Calero Salazar could be released. He has remained in solitary confinement. Prosecutors told Kaplan a ruling is expected in the next week to 10 days.

Although Calero Salazar is still seeking political asylum in the United States, Deutsch told Kaplan that his client's wife has been granted asylum in Denmark and that Calero Salazar would agree to be deported there. However, he has not gotten official word whether Denmark would accept him.
Kaplan said he would withhold ruling for several reasons including confirmation of an official decision by Denmark.
Calero Salazar had originally been detained when he went to the INS office to seek political asylum on May 30.
A Peruvian farmer who had been living with his sisters in Connecticut, Calero Salazar was detained because he had entered the United States illegally.
While in detention, he was arrested June 3 on a separate federal criminal complaint based on a Peruvian arrest warrant.
Federal prosecutors said he had been indicted on "terrorism" charges in Peru and there were five outstanding warrants for his arrest there.
They said Peru alleged that he was a member of the Shining Path group, which had planned and executed many attacks in Peru, resulting in the deaths of police officers and civilians.
